Aim and objectives

Aim. To prepare you to explain the integrated neurobiology of autism, ADHD, addiction, anxiety, PTSD and OCD for MRCPsych Paper A.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Describe the high heritability of autism and synaptic genes, and delayed cortical maturation and catecholamine signalling in ADHD.
  2. Explain addiction through mesolimbic dopamine from the ventral tegmental area to the nucleus accumbens, and opponent adaptation.
  3. Describe the anxiety circuit: an overactive amygdala with weak prefrontal control.
  4. Explain PTSD neurobiology, including amygdala hyperactivity, reduced ventromedial prefrontal control and HPA axis changes.
  5. Describe cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical loop and orbitofrontal hyperactivity in OCD.
  6. Answer the chapter's 84 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
